nodes.name: Chloride Corrosion Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Synthesizing multimetallic hydroxide nanosheet arrays supported on NF by fully utilizing a high concentration of chloride ions (Cl⁻) to corrode NF in a one-step route. First, the NF was corroded to Ni²⁺ ions in a high concentration of Cl⁻ solution occurring in the anode region. Then, the chloride ions continuously migrated and enriched the anode region. Simultaneously, the oxygen from the air or water reacted with water to form hydroxide (OH⁻) on the cathode. Finally, the Mˣ⁺ cations and the diffusion of Ni²⁺ synchronously reacted with OH⁻ to precipitate and form multimetallic hydroxide nanosheet arrays supported on NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: The synthesized monometallic (Ni(OH)₂) and bimetallic (e.g., NiCo-OH) hydroxides exhibited no characteristic peak, indicating their amorphous nature. Additionally, the multimetallic (e.g., NiCoMo-OH) hydroxides exhibited a wide weak peak at around 25°, revealing the low crystallinity of these multimetallic hydroxide nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline nature of hydroxide nanosheets was analyzed via X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure S5). The synthesized monometallic (Ni(OH)₂) and bimetallic (e.g., NiCo-OH) hydroxides exhibited no characteristic peak, indicating their amorphous nature. Additionally, the multimetallic (e.g., NiCoMo-OH) hydroxides exhibited a wide weak peak at around 25°, revealing the low crystallinity of these multimetallic hydroxide nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: For NiCo-OH, NiMo-OH, and Ni₅Co₃Mo-OH: Ni 2p₃/₂ at 855.6 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 873.2 eV with satellites at 861.6 and 879.6 eV indicate Ni²⁺. Co 2p₃/₂ at 781.1 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 796.8 eV indicate Co²⁺ and Co³⁺. Mo 3d at 231.7 eV (Mo⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂) and 234.9 eV (Mo⁶⁺ 3d₃/₂). O 1s at 531 eV for metal-oxygen bonds. Mo 3d and O 1s binding energies shift lower in Ni₅Co₃Mo-OH vs NiMo-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ni 2p spectra of NiCo-OH, NiMo-OH, and Ni₅Co₃Mo-OH, 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ peaks were situated at 855.6 and 873.2 eV (Figure 3a). ... the spectra of Mo 3d include two energy bands located at 231.7 and 234.9 eV, revealing the coexistence of Mo⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂ and Mo⁶⁺ 3d₃/₂, respectively (Figure 3c). For O 1s spectra ... the peaks at 531 eV are typical metal-oxygen bonds (Figure 3d). ... the binding energies of Mo 3d and O 1s for Ni₅Co₃Mo-OH moved to lower binding energies, which are in comparison with the bimetallic NiMo-OH hydroxide.
